504	This Exhibit B sets forth the valuation policy applicable to the investments of Cascade Structured Credit Fund III, LP (the \"Fund\"). Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Investment Advisory Agreement, dated as of September 27, 2024, to which this Exhibit B is attached (the \"Agreement\").
505	
506	**Section 1 --- General Principles**
507	
508	The Fund\'s investments shall be valued in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (\"U.S. GAAP\") and the Financial Accounting Standards Board (\"FASB\") Accounting Standards Codification Topic 820 --- Fair Value Measurement (\"ASC 820\"). The Adviser shall be responsible for determining the fair value of the Fund\'s investments on a quarterly basis, subject to the oversight of the LPAC and the review of the Auditor (Ridgeline Audit Partners LLP). Fair value shall be determined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date, in accordance with ASC 820. The Adviser shall adopt and maintain written valuation procedures consistent with this Valuation Policy and shall update such procedures as necessary to reflect changes in applicable accounting standards or market practices.
509	
510	**Section 2 --- Fair Value Hierarchy**
511	
512	In accordance with ASC 820, the Fund shall classify its investments within the following fair value hierarchy:
513	
514	> \(a\) **Level 1** --- Valuations based on quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities. It is not anticipated that the Fund will hold a material portion of its portfolio in Level 1 investments.
515	>
516	> \(b\) **Level 2** --- Valuations based on inputs other than quoted prices included in Level 1 that are obs

515:> \(b\) **Level 2** --- Valuations based on inputs other than quoted prices included in Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly (e.g., as prices) or indirectly (e.g., derived from prices). Level 2 inputs include quoted prices for similar assets in active markets, quoted prices for identical or similar assets in markets that are not active, and other observable market data.
517:> \(c\) **Level 3** --- Valuations based on unobservable inputs that reflect the Adviser\'s own assumptions about the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability. Given the Fund\'s strategy of investing primarily in senior secured and unitranche loans to middle-market companies, the majority of the Fund\'s investments are expected to be classified as Level 3 assets. Level 3 valuations require the exercise of significant judgment by the Adviser.
> \(b\) **Level 2** --- Valuations based on inputs other than quoted prices included in Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly (e.g., as prices) or indirectly (e.g., derived from prices). Level 2 inputs include quoted prices for similar assets in active markets, quoted prices for identical or similar assets in markets that are not active, and other observable market data.
>
> \(c\) **Level 3** --- Valuations based on unobservable inputs that reflect the Adviser\'s own assumptions about the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability. Given the Fund\'s strategy of investing primarily in senior secured and unitranche loans to middle-market companies, the majority of the Fund\'s investments are expected to be classified as Level 3 assets. Level 3 valuations require the exercise of significant judgment by the Adviser.

**Section 3 --- Valuation Procedures**

The Adviser shall conduct formal valuations of the Fund\'s investment portfolio on a quarterly basis, as of the last day of each fiscal quarter. The Adviser\'s valuation procedures shall include the following:

> \(a\) **Internal Valuation Committee.** The Adviser shall maintain an internal valuation committee (the \"Valuation Committee\") consisting of senior investment professionals of the Adviser. The Valuation Committee shall review and approve the fair value of each investment on a quarterly basis. The Valuation Committee shall meet no less frequently than quarterly and shall maintain minutes of its proceedings.
>
> \(b\) **Valuation Methodologies.** The Adviser shall employ one or more of the following valuation methodologies, as appropriate for each investment: (i) discounted cash flow analysis, (ii) comparable company analysis, (iii) comparable transaction analysis, (iv) market quotes or indicative bids from dealers or brokers, and (v) such other methodologies as the Valuation Committee deems appropriate and consistent with ASC 820.
>
> \(c\) **Independent Third-Party Valuation Agents.** For any single investment that represents more than ten percent (10%) of the Fund\'s net asset value at the time of valuation, the Adviser shall engage an independent third-party valuation agent to provide an independent assessment of fair value. The Adviser shall consider the independent valuation agent\'s assessment in determining the final fair value of such investment, but shall not be bound by such assessment.
>
> \(d\) **Documentation.** The Adviser shall maintain detailed documentation of the valuation process for each investment, including the valuation methodology employed, key inputs and assumptions, any independent third-party valuation reports obtained, and the basis for the Valuation Committee\'s final determination of fair value.

**Section 4 --- Quarterly Valuation Summary**

The Adviser shall provide to the LPAC a quarterly valuation summary within forty-five (45) Business Days after the end of each fiscal quarter, including: (a) a description of the valuation methodology applied to each Level 3 asset; (b) comparable transaction data utilized in determining fair value; (c) any independent third-party valuation reports obtained during the quarter; and (d) a reconciliation of beginning and ending fair values for each Level 3 investment, including unrealized gains and losses, new investments, dispositions, and other changes. Such quarterly valuation summary shall be delivered in a format reasonably acceptable to the LPAC and shall provide sufficient detail to enable the LPAC to assess the reasonableness of the Adviser\'s valuations.

**Section 5 --- Independent Valuation**

At least annually, the Adviser shall engage an independent third-party valuation firm to conduct a comprehensive review of the fair values of all Level 3 assets held by the Fund. The independent valuation firm shall be a nationally recognized firm with expertise in the valuation of private credit instruments. The results of such annual independent valuation review shall be made available to the LPAC and shall be considered by the Auditor in connection with the annual audit of the Fund\'s financial statements delivered pursuant to Section 7.2 of the Agreement.

**[EXHIBIT C]{.underline}**

**[INVESTMENT GUIDELINES]{.underline}**

This Exhibit C sets forth the investment guidelines applicable to the investment activities of Cascade Structured Credit Fund III, LP (the \"Fund\"). Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Investment Advisory Agreement, dated as of September 27, 2024, to which this Exhibit C is attached (the \"Agreement\").

**Section 1 --- Eligible Investments**

The Fund may invest in the following types of investments, subject to the limitations set forth below:

> \(a\) **Senior Secured Loans.** First lien, senior secured term loans and revolving credit facilities to middle-market companies. Senior secured loans shall comprise the core of the Fund\'s portfolio and are not subject to any allocation limitation.
>
> \(b\) **Unitranche Loans.** Unitranche loans combining senior and subordinated debt tranches into a single credit facility. Unitranche loans shall be treated as senior secured loans for purposes of the Investment Guidelines, provided that the unitranche facility is secured by a first-priority lien on substantially all assets of the borrower.
>
> \(c\) **Second Lien Loans.** Second lien term loans secured by a subordinate lien on the borrower\'s assets. Second lien loans shall not exceed twenty percent (20%) of the Fund\'s aggregate capital commitments, measured at the time of investment.
>
> \(d\) **Mezzanine Debt.** Unsecured or junior secured mezzanine debt instruments. Mezzanine debt investments shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the Fund\'s aggregate capital commitments, measured at the time of investment.
>
> \(e\) **Equity Co-Investments.** Direct or indirect equity co-investments in portfolio companies, including warrants, options, and other equity-linked instruments received in connection with debt investments. Equity co-investments shall not exceed five percent (5%) of the Fund\'s aggregate capital commitments, measured at the time of investment.

**Section 2 --- Geographic Limitations**

The Fund shall invest primarily in companies headquartered in or with principal operations in the United States and Canada. Investments in companies headquartered outside of North America shall not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the Fund\'s aggregate capital commitments, measured at the time of investment.

**Section 3 --- Industry Diversification**

No more than twenty percent (20%) of the Fund\'s aggregate capital commitments shall be invested in any single industry sector, as classified by the Global Industry Classification Standard (\"GICS\"). The Adviser shall monitor industry concentration on an ongoing basis and shall take into account industry diversification objectives in its portfolio construction process.

**Section 4 --- Leverage**

Fund-level leverage (including subscription line facilities, NAV-based credit facilities, and any other borrowings incurred at the Fund level) shall not exceed 1.0x total capital commitments. Investment-level leverage (including leverage at the portfolio company level) shall be subject to the Adviser\'s discretion in accordance with the Adviser\'s credit underwriting standards and the overall risk parameters of the Fund.

**Section 5 --- Investment Size**

Individual investments shall generally be targeted between \$15,000,000 and \$75,000,000 in the aggregate (including any follow-on investments in the same borrower or borrower group). The Adviser may make investments outside of this target range in its discretion, subject to the concentration limit set forth in Section 6 below.

**Section 6 --- Concentration Limit and LPAC Notification**

No single investment shall exceed fifteen percent (15%) of Total Commitments without the prior notification of the LPAC. In the event that any single investment exceeds fifteen percent (15%) of Total Commitments:

> \(a\) the Adviser shall notify the LPAC in writing within five (5) Business Days of the date such investment is made; and
>
> \(b\) the Adviser shall provide the LPAC with a written investment memorandum describing the investment, the rationale for exceeding the concentration limit, the Adviser\'s assessment of the risk associated with the concentration, and any mitigating factors.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Adviser shall not be required to obtain LPAC approval prior to making any investment that exceeds the concentration limit; however, the notification obligations set forth above shall apply.

**Section 7 --- Compliance Monitoring**

The Adviser shall monitor compliance with these Investment Guidelines on an ongoing basis. Any material breach of the Investment Guidelines shall be reported to the Limited Partners and the LPAC pursuant to Section 8.3(d) of the Agreement. The Adviser shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cure any such breach as promptly as practicable; provided, that breaches resulting solely from changes in asset values, repayments, or other events occurring after the date of the applicable investment shall not be deemed a breach of these Investment Guidelines so long as the Adviser uses commercially reasonable efforts to bring the portfolio into compliance within a reasonable period of time.

**[EXHIBIT D]{.underline}**

**[SIDE LETTER PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

This Exhibit D sets forth certain provisions that supplement or modify the terms of the Investment Advisory Agreement, dated as of September 27, 2024 (the \"Agreement\"), or the Agreement of Limited Partnership of Cascade Structured Credit Fund III, LP, with respect to specified Limited Partners. This Exhibit D is incorporated by reference into the Agreement pursuant to Section 12.9. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Agreement.

**Section 1 --- General**

The Adviser and/or the General Partner may, in connection with the admission of Limited Partners to the Fund or at any time thereafter, enter into Side Letters granting certain rights, benefits, or privileges to one or more Limited Partners, including without limitation enhanced reporting rights, fee modifications, transfer rights, and other accommodations. The provisions of this Exhibit D summarize the material Side Letter commitments entered into as of the Effective Date. This Exhibit D does not purport to be a complete summary of all Side Letter provisions and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the actual Side Letters on file with the Adviser.

**Section 2 --- Most Favored Nation (MFN) Disclosure**

\(a\) **Initial Disclosure.** The Adviser shall deliver to each Limited Partner copies of all Side Letter provisions (excluding those containing commercially sensitive fee terms that have been designated as confidential by the applicable Limited Partner) within thirty (30) calendar days after the Final Close. Such disclosure shall be sufficient to enable each Limited Partner to exercise its most favored nation election rights, if any, as described in the Agreement of Limited Partnership.

\(b\) **Subsequent Side Letters.** Any Side Letter entered into after the Final Close shall be disclosed to all Limited Partners within fifteen (15) Business Days of execution. Such disclosure shall include a summary of the material terms of such Side Letter (excluding commercially sensitive fee terms) and a statement of the Limited Partner\'s right, if any, to elect to receive the benefit of such terms.

**Section 3 --- Reporting Enhancements for LPAC Members**

In addition to the reports provided to Limited Partners generally under Article 7 of the Agreement, each LPAC member shall be entitled to the enhanced reports set forth in Section 7.6 of the Agreement. Nothing in this Exhibit D limits the Adviser\'s obligations under Section 7.6.

**Section 4 --- Tax-Exempt Investors**

With respect to any Limited Partner that is a tax-exempt entity (including entities described in Section 501(a) or Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code, state and local government pension plans, and other similarly situated entities), the Adviser shall provide the enhanced UBTI reporting described in Section 7.5 of the Agreement and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to structure investments in a manner that minimizes unrelated business taxable income to such tax-exempt Limited Partners, to the extent consistent with the Fund\'s investment strategy and the Adviser\'s fiduciary duties to the Fund and all Limited Partners.

**Section 5 --- Sovereign Bridge Insurance Co. --- Enhanced Reporting**

In recognition of the regulatory requirements applicable to Sovereign Bridge Insurance Co. as a domestic insurance company regulated by a state department of insurance, the Adviser agrees to provide the following enhanced reporting to Sovereign Bridge Insurance Co.:

\(a\) **Monthly NAV Estimates.** The Adviser shall deliver to Sovereign Bridge Insurance Co. monthly NAV estimates within twenty (20) calendar days after the end of each calendar month. Such NAV estimates shall include the Fund\'s estimated net asset value as of the last day of such month, calculated using available data and reasonable estimates, and shall be accompanied by a summary of material changes in portfolio composition since the prior month-end. The Adviser acknowledges that such monthly NAV estimates are preliminary in nature and are subject to revision upon completion of the Fund\'s quarterly financial statements. Sovereign Bridge Insurance Co. acknowledges that such monthly NAV estimates are based on information available at the time of preparation and that actual results may differ materially from such estimates.

\(b\) **Quarterly Regulatory Capital Impact Analysis.** The Adviser shall provide Sovereign Bridge Insurance Co. with a quarterly regulatory capital impact analysis in a format reasonably acceptable to Sovereign Bridge Insurance Co. within sixty (60) calendar days after the end of each fiscal quarter. Such analysis shall include data sufficient for Sovereign Bridge Insurance Co. to assess the impact of its investment in the Fund on its statutory capital and risk-based capital calculations, including asset classification data, NAIC designations (to the extent available), credit quality assessments, and such other information as may be reasonably requested by Sovereign Bridge Insurance Co. for purposes of its statutory financial reporting.

**Section 6 --- Non-U.S. Investors --- FATCA/CRS**

With respect to any non-U.S. Limited Partner, the Adviser shall cooperate with such Limited Partner in providing such information and documentation as may be reasonably requested to comply with FATCA, the CRS, and any applicable intergovernmental agreements. The obligations of the Adviser under Section 9.5 of the Agreement shall apply in full to any non-U.S. Limited Partner.

**Section 7 --- ERISA Investors**

With respect to any Limited Partner that qualifies as a Benefit Plan Investor, the provisions of Section 9.2 of the Agreement shall apply in full. The Adviser shall cooperate with any such Limited Partner\'s reasonable requests for additional information necessary for such Limited Partner to comply with its fiduciary obligations under ERISA.

**Section 8 --- Apex State Pension System --- Specific Provisions**

In recognition of the regulatory requirements and governance standards applicable to Apex State Pension System as a public pension fund:

\(a\) **Placement Agent Disclosure Certificates.** The Adviser shall provide Apex State Pension System with quarterly placement agent disclosure certificates within thirty (30) calendar days after the end of each fiscal quarter, certifying in a form reasonably acceptable to Apex State Pension System compliance with the Adviser\'s representations regarding placement agents and political contributions in connection with the Fund. Such certificates shall cover the fiscal quarter then ended and shall be delivered via the Investor Portal or by electronic mail to Apex State Pension System\'s designated contact.

\(b\) **FOIA Compliance Certificates.** The Adviser shall provide Apex State Pension System with annual Freedom of Information Act compliance certificates within ninety (90) calendar days after the end of each Fiscal Year, confirming the Adviser\'s awareness that Apex State Pension System may be subject to public records requests under applicable state and federal freedom of information and open records laws, and certifying that the Adviser has identified all information provided to Apex State Pension System during the preceding Fiscal Year that the Adviser considers to be confidential, proprietary, or otherwise subject to a claim of exemption from disclosure under applicable public records laws.

**Section 9 --- Clarkfield Family Office and Northshore Endowment Fund**

No enhanced reporting provisions are provided with respect to Clarkfield Family Office or Northshore Endowment Fund beyond those provided to all Limited Partners and LPAC members generally under Article 7 and Section 7.6 of the Agreement. Standard LPAC information rights under Section 7.6 of the Agreement apply.

*\[End of Exhibit D\]*

ISSUES = [
(1, "Critical", "Sequencing / Administrator feasibility", "§7.4 vs. §7.1; SLA §§2, 3, 7",
 "Quarterly capital account statements (45 days) cannot be produced on Pinnacle’s SLA and are due before the financial statements on which they depend",
 "§7.4 requires LP capital account statements within 45 calendar days of quarter-end, while the §7.1 quarterly financial statements (which include the statement of changes in partners’ capital) are due at Day 60. Capital account allocations of income, loss and Management Fee depend on fund-level income and expense determinations — Pinnacle states expressly that capital account statements ‘cannot be finalized until the quarterly financial data package is complete’ (SLA §3). Pinnacle’s cascade is: preliminary NAV at Day 35 (Day 40 for the initial quarter), which itself requires the Adviser’s final marks by Day 25; finalized data package 5 Business Days after Adviser sign-off; draft capital account statements 7 Business Days after that; Adviser review; Portal upload 2 Business Days after receipt of final versions. Assuming a 2–3 Business Day Adviser sign-off, statements reach the Portal around Day 58 in a standard quarter (e.g., Thu Feb 27 equivalent) and around Thu Mar 6, 2025 for Q4 2024 — roughly three weeks after the Fri Feb 14, 2025 contractual date. The shortfall is structural and recurs every quarter, not only in the launch quarter. The ordering inversion also means LPs would see LP-level figures before the fund-level statements they reconcile to.",
 "(a) Seek an amendment aligning §7.4 to 60 calendar days (same day as §7.1), via a written IAA amendment under §12.4 with any LP consent the LPA requires — an LPAC memorandum alone cannot reduce a right owed to every LP (see Part VII). (b) Pending amendment, negotiate with Pinnacle to compress the cascade (Adviser marks by Day 20; preliminary NAV by Day 30; parallel preparation of draft capital statements from the preliminary NAV; sign-off within 2 Business Days). (c) As a fallback for Q4 2024, deliver on Feb 14 an ‘estimated’ capital account statement clearly labelled preliminary and subject to the §7.1 statements and audit, with a cover notice — this mitigates but does not cure a technical breach; disclose proactively to the LPAC."),
(2, "High", "Body vs. exhibit deadline conflict", "§7.6(b) vs. Ex. B §4; §12.9",
 "Quarterly valuation reporting to the LPAC: 45 calendar days (body) vs. 45 Business Days (Exhibit B), with differing content",
 "§7.6(b) requires a Level 3 ‘valuation report’ within 45 calendar days; Ex. B §4 requires a ‘quarterly valuation summary’ within 45 Business Days — roughly 63–65 calendar days (Q4 2024: Fri Feb 14, 2025 vs. Fri Mar 7, 2025; Q1 2025: Thu May 15 vs. Tue Jun 3, 2025). The content also differs: Ex. B adds comparable transaction data, third-party valuation reports and a Level 3 roll-forward reconciliation, while §7.6(b) adds key inputs/assumptions, methodology changes and material adjustments. These are best read as the same underlying obligation described twice. Under §12.9, the body controls over an exhibit in a conflict, so the operative deadline is 45 calendar days; Exhibit B’s content requirements are not inconsistent with the body and should be treated as cumulative. A Level 3 roll-forward at Day 45 depends on Pinnacle data (preliminary NAV Day 35/40), so the window is tight but achievable if the Valuation Committee completes marks by Day 25.",
 "Calendar a single combined LPAC valuation report at 45 calendar days containing the union of §7.6(b) and Ex. B §4 content. Correct Ex. B §4 to ‘calendar days’ in a conforming amendment (LPAC approval is required for Valuation Policy amendments per the §1.1 definition). Address in the LPAC clarifying memorandum so no member relies on the later date."),
(3, "Critical", "Administrator feasibility / immediate deadline", "Ex. D §5(a); §7.6(a); SLA §2",
 "Sovereign Bridge monthly NAV estimates are due at Day 20; Pinnacle’s monthly NAV estimate is not available until Day 25 — and the October and November 2024 estimates are due now",
 "Ex. D §5(a) requires monthly NAV estimates within 20 calendar days of month-end. Pinnacle commits only to Day 25 monthly estimates (SLA §2), which are themselves based on Adviser-provided monthly marks. The Adviser therefore must produce the Sovereign estimate itself, from its own marks, before Pinnacle’s figure exists — or renegotiate Pinnacle’s timeline. The first estimate (October 2024) was due Wed Nov 20, 2024, one week after Sovereign’s inquiry; November is due Fri Dec 20, 2024 (Pinnacle’s November estimate would fall on Dec 25); December is due Mon Jan 20, 2025 (a bank holiday), before the Q4 Valuation Committee process and Pinnacle’s Day 25 mark deadline are complete, so the quarter-end estimate will necessarily diverge from the Q4 formal valuation. Sovereign is building regulatory capital models from this data, so revisions should be explained. Ex. D §5(a) also requires a ‘summary of material changes in portfolio composition’, which Pinnacle does not supply.",
 "(a) Immediately deliver the October 2024 estimate (late) with a brief cover note, and the November estimate by Dec 20, 2024, prepared in-house from the §7.6(a) monthly marks. (b) Ask Pinnacle for a Day 15–18 ‘flash’ NAV for Sovereign as an SLA amendment (custom formatting needs 15 Business Days’ notice per SLA §3). (c) Standardize a short methodology note and revision reconciliation to the quarterly statements. (d) Respond to Sovereign’s inquiry with the data flow and timeline in Part VIII."),
(4, "Critical", "Administrator feasibility / undefined term", "§7.5(b); Ex. D §4; SLA §4",
 "UBTI estimates due Day 30, but Pinnacle provides UBTI data only on Day 45 and will not prepare interim estimates",
 "§7.5(b) requires UBTI estimates for each tax-exempt LP within 30 calendar days of Fiscal Year-end (Thu Jan 30, 2025). Pinnacle delivers UBTI worksheets only within the Day 45 tax data package (Fri Feb 14, 2025), expressly does not prepare standalone interim UBTI estimates, and for the first partial tax year ‘cannot guarantee earlier delivery of any component, including UBTI data’ (SLA §4). Compounding the problem, the Adviser’s own investment-level tax characterization inputs to Pinnacle (OID, loan modifications, fee income) are due Day 30 — the same day the UBTI estimate is due to LPs. Interpretive gaps: Ex. D §4 calls this ‘enhanced UBTI reporting described in Section 7.5’ but §7.5(b) describes only the standard estimate; Ex. D §4’s tax-exempt definition (501(c)(3), state/local government pension plans, ‘similarly situated entities’) is broader than §7.5(b)’s (501(a) ‘including without limitation’); and ‘if any’ leaves open whether a nil estimate must be sent. For a direct-lending fund, UBTI exposure typically arises from fund-level leverage (debt-financed income) and from any fee or equity-kicker income, so subscription-line borrowings since First Close are relevant.",
 "(a) Have the Adviser’s tax preparer produce an independent UBTI estimate by Jan 30, 2025 from Adviser data (borrowing history, fee income), clearly labelled preliminary per §7.5(b). (b) Send a written estimate (including ‘nil’, if so) to every tax-exempt LP identified under the broader Ex. D §4 definition. (c) Clarify ‘enhanced’ and the tax-exempt definition in the LPAC memorandum/side letter amendment. (d) Seek Pinnacle agreement to an interim UBTI schedule by Day 25 going forward."),
(5, "High", "Administrator feasibility", "§9.2(a); SLA §§6, 7",
 "Quarterly BPI calculation due Day 30, but Pinnacle provides it only in the Day 35 (Day 40 initial quarter) package",
 "§9.2(a) requires quarterly Benefit Plan Investor percentage calculations to each BPI and the LPAC within 30 calendar days of quarter-end (Q4 2024: Thu Jan 30, 2025). Pinnacle delivers the calculation as part of the quarterly financial data package at Day 35 (Day 40 for the initial quarter). Because the BPI percentage changes only on closings, transfers and redemptions, not on valuation, the calculation does not need the quarterly NAV and can be performed in-house from subscription data.",
 "Prepare the BPI calculation internally from the investor register by Day 25, with Pinnacle’s Day 35 figure used as a reconciliation check; alternatively, amend the SLA to deliver the BPI calculation separately by Day 20. Low-cost fix; no IAA amendment needed."),
(6, "High", "Sequencing / Administrator feasibility", "§7.5(a); SLA §4",
 "K-1 timeline: the March 15 target is unlikely to be met and the February 28 notice-and-estimate obligation will likely be triggered",
 "Pinnacle’s tax data package arrives Day 45 (Fri Feb 14, 2025); the preparer then needs 15–20 Business Days for draft K-1s (Mon Mar 10 – Mon Mar 17, 2025), before Adviser review. from issues1 import ISSUES

(10, "Medium", "Internal inconsistency", "§7.3",
 "Annual report must both ‘accompany the meeting notice’ (≥30 calendar days before the meeting) and be delivered ‘no later than 15 Business Days’ before it",
 "The two timing rules in §7.3 are not coextensive: the notice must go out at least 30 calendar days before the meeting, and the annual report must accompany it, yet a separate outside date of 15 Business Days (about 21 calendar days) is also stated. Read together, the stricter ‘accompany the notice’ requirement governs; the 15-Business-Day test is only a backstop if the meeting is rescheduled. For FY2024, a meeting on Fri Jun 27, 2025 requires notice and annual report by Wed May 28, 2025. The annual report also requires full-year performance metrics and an ESG report, which compete with the April audit and K-1 workload.",
 "Calendar the annual report with the notice (target mid-May 2025). Clarify in the LPAC memorandum that the report will accompany the notice. Consider holding the meeting earlier (e.g., early June) to free up the end-June window."),
(11, "Medium", "Overlapping / internally inconsistent provisions", "§8.4(b) vs. §8.4(c); Rule 204-3",
 "Form ADV Part 2A: 5-Business-Day notice of ‘any amendment’ vs. annual delivery within 120 days ‘or promptly upon any material amendment, whichever is earlier’",
 "§8.4(b) requires notice within 5 Business Days of any Brochure amendment (material or not); §8.4(c) requires annual delivery within 120 days of Fiscal Year-end (day-count basis unstated) or ‘promptly’ upon material amendment, ‘whichever is earlier’. Because the Adviser’s annual updating amendment must be filed within 90 days of its fiscal year-end, §8.4(b) will in practice require delivery within 5 Business Days of that filing (Mon Apr 7, 2025 if filed Mar 31), making the 120-day outside date in §8.4(c) largely illusory and ‘promptly’ superseded by the 5-Business-Day rule. §8.4(c) also measures from the Fund’s Fiscal Year rather than the Adviser’s (Rule 204-3 runs from the adviser’s fiscal year-end). Delivery methods differ (§8.4(c) specifies Portal or e-mail; §8.4(b) is silent).",
 "Operate to the strictest reading: deliver the amended Brochure (or summary of material changes) via Portal and e-mail within 5 Business Days of every filing, including other-than-annual amendments. Confirm the Adviser’s fiscal year-end. Address via conforming clarification."),
(12, "Medium", "Overlapping triggers / Administrator dependency", "§8.3; §8.1(f); Art. 6; §9.4; SLA §5",
 "Overlapping event-notice provisions with different recipients, clocks and triggers; Administrator cyber incidents",
 "The same event can trigger several notices: an Adviser financial deterioration triggers ‘prompt’ notice to the Fund and LPAC (§8.1(f)) and 10-Business-Day notice to all LPs (§8.3(a)); misappropriation triggers ‘prompt’ LPAC notice (Art. 6) and potentially §8.3(c) or (e). ‘Promptly’ is undefined and may be read as shorter than 10 Business Days. §8.3’s clock runs from ‘occurrence’, not discovery, and §8.3(e) covers cybersecurity incidents affecting the Administrator — but the Pinnacle SLA contains no incident-notification commitment, so the Adviser could be in breach before it knows of the incident. §8.3 requires BOTH e-mail and Portal posting; posting alone is insufficient. ‘Material’ is undefined throughout.",
 "Adopt an internal escalation procedure: LPAC notified within 2 Business Days of any §8.3 event, all LPs within 10 Business Days, both channels. Seek a contractual incident-notice covenant from Pinnacle (e.g., 48 hours) in the Services Agreement. Consider clarifying §8.3 to run from the Adviser’s knowledge."),
(13, "Medium", "Internal inconsistency / moving threshold", "Ex. C §6; Ex. C §5; §8.3(d)",
 "Concentration limit: ‘prior notification’ language vs. 5-Business-Day post-investment notice; denominator moves with closings",
 "The lead-in to Ex. C §6 says no investment shall exceed 15% of Total Commitments ‘without the prior notification of the LPAC’, but clause (a) permits notice within 5 Business Days after the investment is made and the final sentence confirms no prior approval is needed. ‘Total Commitments’ grows with each closing: the threshold is $61.8 million at $412 million, below the $75 million top of the Ex. C §5 target size range, rising to $112.5 million at $750 million. It is unclear whether the test is measured at the time of investment (as for other Ex. C limits) and whether follow-ons aggregate (Ex. C §5 suggests they do). No deadline applies to the investment memorandum.",
 "Give notice before closing wherever practicable (satisfying both readings) and in no event later than 5 Business Days after funding, with the memorandum delivered simultaneously. Clarify measurement date and aggregation in the LPAC memorandum."),
(14, "Medium", "Calendar convention", "§§7.1, 7.2, 7.6, 9.2, 9.5; Ex. D; SLA §5",
 "No weekend/holiday roll convention for calendar-day deadlines; Portal upload lead time",
 "The IAA counts most deadlines in calendar days without stating what happens when the last day falls on a weekend or holiday. Several FY2024 dates do: §7.1 and Ex. D §5(b) (Sat Mar 1, 2025), K-1 target (Sat Mar 15), Sovereign December NAV (Mon Jan 20, MLK Day), annual meeting outside date (Sun Jun 29), LPAC October report (Sat Nov 30). Absent a convention, the conservative assumption is that the deadline is not extended. In addition, Pinnacle uploads Adviser-approved documents within 2 Business Days of receipt, so final documents must reach Pinnacle at least 2 Business Days before every Portal deadline.",
 "Calendar every deadline to the preceding Business Day and build a 2-Business-Day Pinnacle upload buffer (or deliver by e-mail in parallel). Add a business-day convention in the conforming amendment."),
(15, "Low", "Definition", "§1.1 ‘Business Day’; §7.7",
 "‘Business Day’ ambiguity for Federal Reserve holidays on which many Denver banks open",
 "Business Day excludes days on which Denver commercial banks are ‘authorized or required by law to be closed’. Banks are generally authorized to close on Federal Reserve holidays such as Columbus Day and Veterans Day even though many open. This affects 5- and 10-Business-Day deadlines (e.g., First Close Portal credentials: Tue Oct 15 vs. Wed Oct 16, 2024). Pinnacle needs 3 Business Days after receipt of completed onboarding documentation to activate Portal accounts, so the Adviser must transmit onboarding packages within about 7 Business Days of each admission to meet §7.7.",

B §3(c)) undefined; (iii) ‘Level 3’ used in §7.6(b) but defined only in Ex. B §2(c); (iv) ‘material’ (conflict, breach, cybersecurity incident, compliance change, amendment) undefined; (v) ‘Benefit Plan Investor percentage’ and ‘class of equity interest’ (whether the GP interest is a class) not specified; (vi) ‘enhanced UBTI reporting’ (Ex. D §4) undefined; (vii) ‘tax-exempt entity’ defined differently in §7.5(b) and Ex. D §4; (viii) ‘the Adviser’s representations regarding placement agents and political contributions’ not found in the IAA; (ix) ‘Fund Expenses’ capitalized but undefined (§5.2(b)(i)); (x) ‘Freedom of Information Act’ (federal statute) used for a state pension’s public records obligations; (xi) ‘management letter’ and ‘reasonable time’ (§7.2).",
 "Adopt working definitions in the compliance manual and include clarifications in the LPAC memorandum/conforming amendment."),
(17, "Medium", "Practical / undefined", "Ex. D §8(b); §8.2(c)",
 "Apex ‘FOIA’ certificate requires the Adviser to have identified everything delivered to Apex during the year that it considers confidential",
 "The certificate (due Mon Mar 31, 2025) certifies that the Adviser ‘has identified all information provided to Apex’ in the Fiscal Year that it considers confidential or exempt. This is only possible with a contemporaneous log covering Portal postings, LPAC monthly and quarterly reports, conflict notices, annual meeting materials and ad hoc correspondence. Federal FOIA applies to federal agencies; Apex’s exposure is presumably under its state open-records statute, whose exemptions (often for trade secrets or alternative investment information) determine what can be protected. §8.2(c) already subordinates Apex’s confidentiality obligations to public records laws, so this matrix and any LPAC memorandum shared with Apex may itself become public.",
 "Implement an Apex delivery log now (from Oct 1, 2024), mark documents ‘Confidential – Trade Secret/Proprietary’ at delivery, and identify the governing state statute. Draft the certificate template with the Apex investment office."),
(18, "Medium", "ERISA substance / trigger", "§9.2(a)–(c); Ex. D §7",
 "ERISA reporting: whether any Benefit Plan Investors exist; threshold-notice trigger; meaning of the annual certificate",
 "The LPAC investors are a governmental plan (Apex — governmental plans are generally not Benefit Plan Investors), an endowment, a family office and an insurer. Sovereign may be a BPI to the extent its general or separate account assets include plan assets, which should be confirmed from its subscription documents. If there are no BPIs, it is unclear whether the quarterly calculation must still go to the LPAC (the obligation is framed ‘with respect to any Limited Partner that is a Benefit Plan Investor’ but the recipient list includes the LPAC); we recommend sending it regardless. The 25% test applies on each acquisition of interests, so each closing through Final Close is the relevant test point — a §9.2(b) notice within 10 Business Days after the Fund has already crossed 25% does not avoid plan-asset status. The trigger date (occurrence vs. identification) is unstated. The §9.2(c) certificate of ‘compliance with the applicable provisions of ERISA’ has little content if the Fund is not a plan-asset vehicle.",
 "Confirm BPI status of every LP; run the 25% test before each subsequent closing and transfer; send the quarterly calculation to the LPAC in all events; draft the annual certificate to certify the Fund’s non-plan-asset status and BPI monitoring."),
(19, "Medium", "First-year anomalies / drafting", "§1.1 ‘Fiscal Year’; Recitals; §5.1(c); §7.3; Ex. B §5",
 "Initial Fiscal Year and launch-period issues",
 "(i) The initial Fiscal Year is defined to commence on the Effective Date (Oct 1, 2024), but the Fund was formed Aug 22, 2024 and incurred organizational expenses ($1,087,500 vs. $1,250,000 cap) before then; GAAP and audited statements will run from inception or commencement of operations — confirm the audit period with Ridgeline. (ii) The Recitals state RAUM of $3.2 billion ‘as of December 31, 2024’ in an agreement dated Sept 27, 2024 — an apparent drafting error (likely Dec 31, 2023). (iii) The IAA and SLA describe Oct 1–Dec 31, 2024 as a ‘partial’ quarter, but it is a full calendar quarter; the §5.1(c) proration yields 92/92, i.e., the full $1,545,000, which should be reflected consistently in capital account statements. from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.section import WD_ORIENT
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

NAVY = RGBColor(0x1F,0x2A,0x44)

def shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd"); shd.set(qn("w:val"),"clear"); shd.set(qn("w:color"),"auto"); shd.set(qn("w:fill"),hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(shd)

def repeat_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    el = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader"); el.set(qn("w:val"),"true"); trPr.append(el)

def no_split(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    el = OxmlElement("w:cantSplit"); el.set(qn("w:val"),"true"); trPr.append(el)

def set_cell(cell, text, size=8, bold=False, color=None, italic=False):
    cell.text = ""
    p = cell.paragraphs[0]
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(0)
    parts = text.split("\n")
    for i, part in enumerate(parts):
        if i>0:
            p = cell.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
        r = p.add_run(part); r.font.size = Pt(size); r.bold = bold; r.italic = italic
        if color: r.font.color.rgb = color

def make_table(doc, headers, rows, widths, size=8, header_fill="1F2A44", zebra=True, sev_col=None):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    t.autofit = False
    hdr = t.rows[0]
    repeat_header(hdr)
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        set_cell(hdr.cells[i], h, size=size, bold=True, color=RGBColor(0xFF,0xFF,0xFF))
        shade(hdr.cells[i], header_fill)
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
        cells = t.add_row().cells
        for i,v in enumerate(row):
            set_cell(cells[i], str(v), size=size, bold=(i==0))
            if zebra and ri%2==1: shade(cells[i], "F2F4F7")
        if sev_col is not None:
            sev = str(row[sev_col])
            fill = {"Critical":"F4C7C3","High":"FCE5CD","Medium":"FFF2CC","Low":"D9EAD3"}.get(sev)
            if fill: shade(cells[sev_col], fill)
    for row in t.rows:
        for i,w in enumerate(widths):
            row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    # tblGrid widths
    grid = t._tbl.tblGrid
    for i, gc in enumerate(grid.findall(qn("w:gridCol"))):
        gc.set(qn("w:w"), str(int(widths[i]*1440)))
    return t

def heading(doc, text, level=1):
    h = doc.add_heading(text, level=level)
    for r in h.runs: r.font.color.rgb = NAVY
